mainTopic: Which flawed גיטין bar a woman from marrying a כהן, and the debate over ברירה (retroactive clarification), including whether it matters if the choice rests on oneself or on others.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא: a חליצה done by a minor, or done with a soft cloth shoe, is invalid and does not disqualify the woman. The גמרא then returns to the flawed גיטין of our משנה. זעירי and רב אסי say none of them bar the woman from marrying a כהן, except the last case, where the husband left open which wife the גט was for. רבי יוחנן says even that case does not bar her, because he does not accept ברירה. The same view shows up in his ruling that brothers who split an inheritance count as buyers. The גמרא explains why he needed to say both rulings. רב הושעיא then asks about a גט for whichever wife leaves the door first. רב יהודה answers from our משנה, and a challenge from a father's קרבן פסח is pushed aside, because there the race was only to make the children eager. Finally, אביי, רבא and רב משרשיא debate whether ברירה depends on whether the choice rests on oneself or on others. The proof from רבי יהודה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A minor or a cloth shoe: the חליצה is invalid and does not disqualify
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by ruling that חליצה done by a minor יבם, or done with a soft cloth shoe, is invalid and does not disqualify the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the יבם was a minor, or the חליצה was done with a soft cloth shoe, the חליצה is invalid, and it does not disqualify her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא about flawed חליצה. These last two cases are so flawed that they have no legal effect at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some flawed חליצות are not good enough to free the woman, but they still stop her from doing יבום. A minor or a cloth shoe is weaker still. Such a חליצה does nothing, so the woman stays fully able to marry the יבם. This sets up the same question for flawed גיטין: which ones still have a legal effect?

keyTerms.meaning: A minor (here, a יבם who is not yet an adult)
A soft cloth shoe, not the proper shoe for חליצה
Invalid; they do not work as a proper חליצה
They do not disqualify; they have no restricting effect

steps.confusionAlert: Being 'invalid' (פסולה) and 'disqualifying' (פוסלת) are two different things. Some acts fail to work, yet still create a restriction. These two cases do neither.

phrases.english: A minor, or a soft cloth shoe:
phrases.notes: 'Minor' means the יבם is a child; the cloth shoe means the חליצה was done without the proper shoe.

phrases.english: these are invalid, and they do not disqualify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא on flawed חליצה that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חליצה by a minor or with a cloth shoe is invalid and has no disqualifying effect.

steps.title: זעירי: only the last case of the משנה disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: זעירי rules that none of the flawed גיטין in the משנה bar the woman from כהונה, except the final case.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said: none of them disqualify, except the last one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the flawed גיטין listed in our משנה. It asks which of them still bar the woman from marrying a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of the flawed גיטין in the משנה were never truly written for this woman, so they mean nothing for her. In the last case, the husband had the גט written for 'whichever wife I choose.' That גט might count as hers once he chooses. Because of that doubt, it disqualifies her from כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose ruling is quoted here
All of them (all the cases in the משנה)
Except the last one (the final case in the משנה)

phrases.english: Ze'eiri said:
none of them disqualify,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the flawed גיטין in our משנה, and 'disqualify' means stopping her from marrying a כהן.

phrases.english: except the last one.
phrases.notes: The last case is where the husband said he would decide later which wife gets the גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְעֵירִי אָמַר כּוּלָּן אֵין פּוֹסְלִין חוּץ מִן הָאַחֲרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from flawed חליצה back to the flawed גיטין of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Of the משנה's flawed גיטין, only the final case (the undecided choice of wife) bars the woman from כהונה.

steps.title: רב אסי agrees with זעירי
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי gives the same ruling: none of the cases disqualify except the last.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אסי said the same: none of them disqualify, except the last one.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא, רב אסי, backs up זעירי's ruling word for word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two authorities now agree that the last case is different. That case is uncertain, so it is treated strictly. This sets up רבי יוחנן's disagreement in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly said (introduces an agreeing opinion)
An אמורא who agrees with זעירי here

phrases.english: And similarly, Rav Asi said:
none of them disqualify,
except the last one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports זעירי's ruling with a matching opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same as זעירי: only the final case disqualifies.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even the last case does not disqualify
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees and holds that even the final case does not bar the woman from כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוחנן said: even the last one does not disqualify.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with זעירי and רב אסי about the last case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the husband's later choice cannot reach back and make the גט count as written for this wife. So the last גט is just as empty as the others, and it has no effect on her.

keyTerms.meaning: Even... also
Does not disqualify

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
even the last one also does not disqualify.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר אַף אַחֲרוֹן נָמֵי אֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the exception made by זעירי and רב אסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No flawed גט in the משנה, not even the final case, bars the woman from כהונה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is consistent: brothers who split an inheritance are buyers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's view fits his ruling that brothers who divide an inheritance count as buyers and must return the land at יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning. רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: brothers who divided an inheritance are considered buyers, and they return the portions to each other in the יובל year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to another ruling of רבי יוחנן to show that his opinion here follows a consistent principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When brothers divide their father's land, one could say ברירה shows that each brother inherited his share directly from their father. רבי יוחנן does not say this. He treats each brother as buying his share from the others, so the land goes back to joint ownership at יובל. In the same way, a later choice cannot make the גט count as written for one particular wife.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning (is consistent with another ruling of his)
Brothers who divided (an inherited estate)
Buyers
The Jubilee year, when bought land returns to its original owners
Retroactive clarification: a later choice reveals what was true from the start

steps.whatToRemember: זעירי and רב אסי treat the 'whichever wife I choose' גט as possibly valid through ברירה, so it disqualifies. רבי יוחנן rejects ברירה, as shown by his inheritance ruling, so even that גט has no effect.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links a divorce law to a basic principle, ברירה, that comes up across many areas of הלכה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan follows his own reasoning,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
brothers who divided an inheritance
are considered buyers,
phrases.notes: Each brother is treated as if he bought his share from the others, not as if he got it straight from their father.

phrases.english: and they return the portions to each other in the Jubilee year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds רבי יוחנן's ruling in his consistent rejection of ברירה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that even the final case does not disqualify.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling, quoted by רבי אסי, that brothers who divide an inheritance are buyers and return the land at יובל.

steps.title: Why the divorce ruling alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that if רבי יוחנן had ruled 'no בְּרֵירָה' only about a גט, we might have limited it to a גט. A גט must be written לִשְׁמָהּ, while the יובל law might apply only to a sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both rulings are needed. If he had said it only about a גט, we would think the reason is that a גט must be written 'for her', meaning for her sake. But in the land case, the תורה said only a sale goes back at יובל, not an inheritance or a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן needed to say the same principle twice. Here it shows that the גט ruling alone would not teach the inheritance ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a גט there is a special reason to reject בְּרֵירָה: the פסוק requires it to be written specifically for her. By contrast, an inheritance is not a sale, so we might think the land never goes back at יובל. Only an explicit ruling about brothers teaches that they count as buyers.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary, meaning both statements are needed
Clarifying something later and treating it as if it was decided from the start
For her sake, meaning written specifically for this woman
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
The Jubilee year, when sold fields go back to their original owners

phrases.english: And it is necessary (to state both rulings);
for if it had been stated only in this case (the גט),

phrases.aramaic: בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּאֵין בְּרֵירָה,
phrases.english: we would say: in this case רבי יוחנן says there is no retroactive clarification,
because we require 'for her', meaning for her sake;
but there (in the inheritance case),
it is a sale that the Merciful One said
should go back at יובל,
but an inheritance or a gift does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question of why רבי יוחנן's two rulings, the one in Step 4 and the one shown in Step 5, are both needed
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case has its own special reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גט ruling might be based only on the requirement of לִשְׁמָהּ, so it would not apply to inheritance
steps.terutzMaskana: The inheritance ruling has to be stated on its own

steps.title: Why the field ruling alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the other direction. If רבי יוחנן had ruled only about a field, we might think it was only a stringency, which by a גט would mean being strict and saying it disqualifies. Or we might think it was a special יובל rule about returning land to how it first was, which says nothing about a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had taught us only about a field, we would say it is because of stringency. Or, alternatively, because land goes back to how it was at the beginning. But here, by a גט, we would say no. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא shows that the field ruling alone would not teach the גט ruling. That finishes the explanation of why both rulings are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The land ruling could be explained without saying there is no בְּרֵירָה at all. Maybe רבי יוחנן is only unsure about בְּרֵירָה and makes the brothers return the land as a stringency. If so, he would also be strict by a גט and say it does disqualify her. Or maybe יובל simply restores all land to the way it was first divided, which has nothing to do with a גט. So the גט ruling, that even the last case does not disqualify, also has to be stated.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught us
As a stringency
As at the beginning, meaning the land returns to how it was first divided

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's 'no בְּרֵירָה' had to be said both for a גט and for brothers' land, because each case has its own possible special reason.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only about a field,
(we would say) it is because it is a stringency;
or alternatively, (the land returns) as it was at the beginning;
phrases.notes: He means that at יובל the land goes back to the way it was first divided among the tribes.

phrases.english: but here (by a גט), say not;
therefore it is necessary (to state both).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא from the other side
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The field ruling might come from treating בְּרֵירָה as a doubt and being strict, which by a גט would mean it does disqualify. Or it might rest on the special יובל rule of returning land to how it was first divided, which does not touch a גט.

steps.title: A גט for whichever wife leaves first
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא asks רב יהודה about a husband who tells the scribe to write a גט for whichever of his wives comes out the door first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא asked רב יהודה: if a man said to a scribe, 'Write a גט for whichever wife comes out the entrance first,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. Who the גט is for depends on an event that happens later, so the question is whether בְּרֵירָה works here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the husband himself does not choose later. An outside event, which wife leaves first, decides. רב הושעיא wants to know whether this is different from a case where the husband picks the wife himself.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him
Scribe
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא מֵרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya asked of Rav Yehuda:
If he said to a scribe:
'Write (a גט) for whichever (wife) comes out the entrance first,'
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא מֵרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about בְּרֵירָה in a גט
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a גט work when the wife is decided by a later event?

steps.title: רב יהודה answers from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says the answer is already in the משנה. Even when the husband says 'for whichever I want,' the גט is invalid, which shows there is no בְּרֵירָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned it. 'Moreover, if he said to the scribe, "Write for whichever one I want, I will divorce," it is unfit to divorce with.' So we see there is no בְּרֵירָה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by pointing to a line in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules a גט invalid when the wife is chosen only later. רב יהודה concludes from this that there is no בְּרֵירָה, so the 'whoever leaves first' case is invalid too.

keyTerms.meaning: You already learned it, meaning it is in a משנה
Moreover, going further than this
Invalid
Apparently, we see from here

phrases.english: He said to him: You already learned it:
Moreover,
if he said to the scribe, 'Write, and whichever one I want I will divorce' –
it is unfit to divorce with;
apparently there is no retroactive clarification!

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גט is invalid, because the משנה shows there is no בְּרֵירָה

steps.title: Challenge from the father's קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא challenges רב יהודה from a משנה. A father slaughters the קרבן פסח for whichever son reaches ירושלים first, and it works. That suggests there is בְּרֵירָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: One who says to his sons, 'I am slaughtering the קרבן פסח for whichever of you goes up to ירושלים first,' once the first one has entered with his head and most of his body, he has acquired his share, and he acquires shares for his brothers along with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא objects to רב יהודה's answer by quoting a משנה that seems to show there is בְּרֵירָה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Who the פסח belongs to is decided only later, by which son arrives first. Yet the משנה treats it as his from the start. That looks like בְּרֵירָה working, which goes against רב יהודה's 'אין ברירה.'

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him from a source
The קרבן פסח, the Passover offering
His head and most of his body
He acquired
He acquires on behalf of others

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
One who says to his sons:
'I am slaughtering the Passover offering

phrases.aramaic: עַל מִי שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה מִכֶּם רִאשׁוֹן לִירוּשָׁלַיִם״;
phrases.english: on behalf of whichever of you goes up first to Jerusalem';
once the first one has entered with his head and most of his body –
he has acquired his portion,
and he acquires for his brothers along with him.

steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's conclusion that there is no בְּרֵירָה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the פסח case, ownership is decided by a later event and still works from the start, which shows יש ברירה

steps.title: The פסח race was only to make the sons eager
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the פסח case is no proof for בְּרֵירָה. According to רבי יוחנן, the father included all the sons from the beginning and only said this to encourage them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: הושעיא, my son, what do פסחים have to do with גיטין? Wasn't it already said about that משנה, in the name of רבי יוחנן, that the father only said this to make his sons eager to do מצוות?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה pushes back on the challenge from step 10. He says the פסח case was never about בְּרֵירָה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the father truly left open which son would get the קרבן פסח. רבי יוחנן explains that all the sons were already included from the start. The 'race' was only a way to motivate them, so nothing in it depends on later clarification.

keyTerms.meaning: to make them eager and quick
the קרבן פסח offerings
bills of divorce
wasn't it already said about it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the son who arrives first is the only one who eats. Everyone was already included; the race was just encouragement.

phrases.english: He said to him: Hoshaya, my son,
phrases.notes: This is רב יהודה answering רב הושעיא.

phrases.english: what do Pesach offerings have to do with bills of divorce?
Wasn't it already said about it,
Rabbi Yochanan said:
it was in order to make them eager in מצוות!
phrases.notes: He means the father had already included all his sons. He only made a race to get them moving.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹשַׁעְיָא בְּרִי, מָה עִנְיַן פְּסָחִים אֵצֶל גִּיטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the פסח משנה in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source: the case does not involve בְּרֵירָה at all.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father left open which son gets the פסח, which would show בְּרֵירָה works.
steps.terutzMaskana: All sons were included from the beginning; the race was only to make them eager for מצוות.

steps.title: The wording of the משנה shows the sons were registered from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves רבי יוחנן's reading from the משנה's words. The first son 'acquires for his brothers', and that only works if they were already registered before the slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact, because the משנה says: once the first son enters ירושלים with his head and most of his body, he acquires his share and acquires for his brothers with him. If the father registered them from the start, that makes sense. But if he did not, can they be registered after the slaughter? We learned that people can join or leave a פסח only until it is slaughtered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבי יוחנן's explanation from the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers get a share too, but a person can only join a קרבן פסח before it is slaughtered. So the brothers must have been registered before the slaughter. That means the father never left it open, and there is no בְּרֵירָה here.

keyTerms.meaning: the wording is also exact (supports this)
his head and most of his body
and acquires for his brothers
he registered them (for the פסח)
people may register for a קרבן פסח

phrases.english: It is also exact in the wording, as it teaches:
once the first one entered with his head and most of his body,

phrases.aramaic: זָכָה בְּחֶלְקוֹ, וּמְזַכֶּה אֶת אֶחָיו עִמּוֹ.
phrases.english: he acquired his portion, and he acquires for his brothers with him.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּאַמְנִינְהוּ מֵעִיקָּרָא – שַׁפִּיר;
phrases.english: Granted, if you say he registered them from the start, it works well;
but if you say he did not register them,
can they be registered after the slaughter?!
But we learned: people may register and withdraw their hands from it,
until it is slaughtered!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's answer in step 11 from the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: That the father included all sons in the פסח from the start.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's phrase 'acquires for his brothers', together with the rule that one can register for a פסח only until it is slaughtered.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the daughters were eager and the sons lazy
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of such a race where the daughters arrived first. It calls the sons lazy but does not say they lost the פסח, so the race was only for encouragement.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: there was an incident where the daughters arrived before the sons, and the daughters were found to be eager and the sons lazy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more support for רבי יוחנן, this time from a ברייתא that tells a story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only criticizes the sons as lazy. It does not say they missed out on the קרבן פסח. That fits the idea that everyone was included and the race was just a test of eagerness.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא also teaches this
an incident, a story that happened
eager, quick (feminine)
lazy, sluggish

steps.whatToRemember: The פסח case is not about בְּרֵירָה. All the children were included from the start, and the race only made them eager for מצוות.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way: There was an incident,
and the daughters came before the sons,
and the daughters were found to be eager and the sons lazy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second support, from a ברייתא, for רבי יוחנן's explanation.
steps.raayaObject: That the פסח race was only meant to make the children eager.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about an incident where the daughters arrived before the sons.

steps.title: אביי: the question, answer and challenge do not match
steps.stepSummary: אביי criticizes the whole exchange. רב הושעיא asked about a choice depending on others. רב יהודה answered from a choice depending on the husband himself. Then רב הושעיא challenged him again from a choice depending on others.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He asked him about someone who makes it depend on what other people decide. He answered him from someone who makes it depend on his own decision. And then he challenged him from someone who makes it depend on what other people decide!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי steps back and points out that the earlier back-and-forth between רב הושעיא and רב יהודה was mismatched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of בְּרֵירָה cases: one depends on another person's action (which wife walks out first), and one depends on the person's own later choice (whichever wife I want). רב הושעיא asked about the first kind. רב יהודה's proof from the משנה was the second kind, so it did not answer the question. Then רב הושעיא's challenge from the פסח went back to the first kind.

keyTerms.meaning: makes it depend on what others decide or do
makes it depend on his own decision
resolves, answers
raises a challenge

steps.confusionAlert: 'Others' here means the wife whose action decides it, like the first one out the door. 'Himself' means the husband choosing later, like 'whichever I want'.
steps.whyThisMatters: אביי introduces a key distinction: בְּרֵירָה that depends on others' actions versus בְּרֵירָה that depends on one's own decision. These may need different rulings.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: קָא בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ תּוֹלֶה בְּדַעַת אֲחֵרִים,
phrases.english: He asks him about one who makes it depend on the decision of others,
phrases.notes: רב הושעיא's question: whichever wife walks out first (step 8).

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא פָשֵׁיט לֵיהּ תּוֹלֶה בְּדַעַת עַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: and he resolves it for him from one who makes it depend on his own decision,
phrases.notes: רב יהודה's answer: 'whichever wife I want' (step 9).

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר מוֹתֵיב לֵיהּ תּוֹלֶה בְּדַעַת אֲחֵרִים!
phrases.english: and then he challenges him from one who makes it depend on the decision of others!
phrases.notes: The פסח case depends on which son arrives first (step 10).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: קָא בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ תּוֹלֶה בְּדַעַת אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the פסח discussion to critique the whole exchange in steps 8-10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The logic of the exchange between רב הושעיא and רב יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The question was about בְּרֵירָה that depends on others. The answer came from בְּרֵירָה that depends on oneself. The challenge then went back to a case that depends on others, so the sides were not dealing with the same kind of case.

steps.title: רבא says the self-versus-others distinction does not matter
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's criticism. Whoever accepts בְּרֵירָה accepts it whether the choice depends on oneself or on others. Whoever rejects it rejects it in both cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the problem? Maybe whoever holds of בְּרֵירָה holds of it no matter whose decision it depends on, and whoever does not hold of it does not hold of it no matter whose decision it depends on.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends the exchange between רב הושעיא and רב יהודה against אביי's complaint. He says there is no mismatch at all, because the type of choice makes no difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי complained that רב יהודה answered a question about 'others' with a case about 'oneself'. רבא says these are not two separate questions. בְּרֵירָה is one single rule, so a proof from either kind of case works for both.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difficulty? A way of saying there is no real problem.
Perhaps, maybe
Something decided later counts as if it had been decided from the start
Making it depend on one's own later decision
Making it depend on someone else's later decision
It makes no difference

phrases.english: Rava said: What is the difficulty?
Perhaps the one who holds of retroactive clarification,
it is no different if one makes it depend on his own decision
and it is no different if one makes it depend on the decision of others,
either way he holds of retroactive clarification.
And the one who does not hold of retroactive clarification,
it is no different if one makes it depend on his own decision
and it is no different if one makes it depend on the decision of others,
either way he does not hold of retroactive clarification!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole of אביי's complaint that the exchange was mismatched
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי assumed בְּרֵירָה works differently depending on whose decision it is. רבא says it is one rule for both.

steps.title: רבי יהודה does distinguish between oneself and others
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא challenges רבא. רבי יהודה rejects בְּרֵירָה when the choice depends on oneself but accepts it when the choice depends on others.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said to רבא: But רבי יהודה holds there is no בְּרֵירָה when it depends on oneself, and there is בְּרֵירָה when it depends on others!
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא challenges רבא's claim that the type of choice makes no difference. He brings רבי יהודה as someone who clearly does make the distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said every opinion treats both kinds of choice the same way. If even one תנא, רבי יהודה, splits them, then the distinction is real, and אביי's criticism stands again. The גמרא will now prove each half of רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... A word that opens a challenge.
He does not hold of it
He holds of it

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said to Rava:
But there is Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתוֹלֶה בְּדַעַת עַצְמוֹ לֵית לֵיהּ בְּרֵירָה,
phrases.english: who, when one makes it depend on his own decision, does not hold of retroactive clarification,

phrases.aramaic: וְתוֹלֶה בְּדַעַת אֲחֵרִים אִית לֵיהּ בְּרֵירָה!
phrases.english: but when one makes it depend on the decision of others, does hold of retroactive clarification!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא לְרָבָא: וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that no opinion distinguishes between choices that depend on oneself and choices that depend on others
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה is a counterexample: he gives different rulings for the two kinds of choice.

steps.title: Proof that רבי יהודה rejects בְּרֵירָה for one's own choice: buying wine from כותים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts proving that רבי יהודה rejects בְּרֵירָה when it depends on oneself. It quotes a ברייתא about a person who buys untithed wine from כותים and names portions he will separate later.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it depends on oneself, he does not hold of בְּרֵירָה, as a ברייתא teaches: Someone who buys wine from the כותים says: Two לוגין that I will separate later are תרומה, ten are מעשר ראשון, and nine are מעשר שני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up the first half of רב משרשיא's claim. It begins quoting a ברייתא, and the ruling of רבי יהודה comes in the continuation of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer has not yet separated anything. He only declares which amounts will become תרומה and מעשר once he takes them out later. Whether that later choice counts from now depends on his own future decision, which is exactly the 'oneself' kind of case.

keyTerms.meaning: Samaritans, who are suspected of not separating תרומה and tithes
A liquid measure (plural of לוֹג)
Will separate in the future
The portion given to a כהן
First tithe, given to a לוי
Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not finished here. רבי יהודה's actual ruling comes in the next lines, so do not look for it yet.

phrases.aramaic: תּוֹלֶה בְּדַעַת עַצְמוֹ לֵית לֵיהּ בְּרֵירָה –
phrases.english: When one makes it depend on his own decision, he does not hold of retroactive clarification,
as it is taught: One who buys wine from among the Samaritans

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵי לוּגִּין שֶׁאֲנִי עָתִיד לְהַפְרִישׁ
phrases.english: says: Two lugin that I will separate in the future
are teruma;
ten are first tithe;
phrases.notes: The words 'that I will separate in the future' carry over to the ten and to the nine as well.

phrases.english: nine are second tithe;
